I will keep cotton as my main crop, because that is the crop system I know best and it fits how I manage my land and labor. My farm is small, only 4.1 mu, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple and put more land into the crop that gives me the best cash return for me, which is cotton. I also grow wheat and maize, so I will still keep some land in those two crops for grain and income balance, but I will not spread myself too thin. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water to protect emergence and key growth stages instead of depending only on rain. I have farmed for 25 years, so I will stay with practical inputs rather than pushing to very high input levels. For cotton, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, several irrigations, and more pesticide sprays because insects are usually the bigger problem there. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it is reliable for yield on small land. For wheat, I will use improved seed, steady fertilizer, and fewer sprays than cotton. I will use rotary tillage on all three because it is the easiest and most manageable way for me to prepare land quickly at the start of the season.
